profile.reading: This site along East 56th Street outside Kearney, in Buffalo County, Nebraska, is tagged in mapping data as a cryptocurrency mining operation under the name Compute North and carries no conventional building footprint, consistent with a mining site built around rows of specialized equipment housed in containers or open sided structures rather than a finished office style building. Compute North was a real bitcoin mining hosting company, headquartered in Minnesota, that built and operated large scale sites across several US states where it housed specialized mining computers, commonly called miners, on behalf of institutional clients and cryptocurrency mining firms. Rather than mining cryptocurrency for its own account, Compute North's business was hosting: it supplied the land, power infrastructure, cooling, security, and technical staff for other companies' mining hardware, charging fees for that hosting and support. The company grew quickly during the 2020 and 2021 boom in cryptocurrency prices and mining investment, expanding its hosting capacity at multiple sites, including locations in Texas, South Dakota, and Nebraska, and signing hosting agreements with major mining firms. That expansion, financed heavily with debt, left the company financially exposed when cryptocurrency prices fell sharply through 2022 while electricity costs rose, squeezing the economics of hosted mining across the industry. Compute North filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September 2022, one of the highest profile failures among a wave of cryptocurrency mining and mining hosting companies that sought bankruptcy protection that year as the market downturn forced out overleveraged operators. Its assets, including hosting contracts, equipment, and site leases, were subsequently sold off or restructured through the bankruptcy process to other operators active in the crypto mining industry. Confirming this Nebraska site's precise present day status, whether it continued operating under a new owner after the bankruptcy, was idled, or was decommissioned and repurposed, was not possible to verify further here: the domain computenorth.com, once the company's corporate website, now redirects to a domain marketplace listing offering it for sale, itself a marker of the company's collapse, but it does not describe what became of any individual site. This entry documents Compute North's confirmed identity as a real, notable bitcoin mining hosting company and its 2022 bankruptcy, while leaving this Nebraska site's current operator and operational status as an open question rather than assuming either way.

reading.body:
Compute North was a Bitcoin mining hosting company headquartered in Minnesota that operated large-scale facilities in several states before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2022. This Nebraska site, tagged in OpenStreetMap as Compute North and reportedly built for cryptocurrency mining rather than conventional colocation, carries a published IT capacity of 30 MW. The facility's current operational status, whether it continues mining under a successor owner, remains idle, or has been decommissioned, could not be confirmed.

Nebraska has 21 mapped data center facilities but publishes no IT capacity figures from operator spec pages. This Compute North site, at 30 MW, ranks first among Nebraska facilities with a published capacity figure. The state context makes clear that most mapped facilities in Nebraska disclose no power figures, so this 30 MW represents an isolated data point rather than a measure of the state's total AI or hosting infrastructure.

At typical Bitcoin mining densities of roughly 10 to 15 kW per rack, 30 MW would support approximately 2,000 to 3,000 racks of mining hardware. This capacity is substantial for a single facility but cannot be counted as active AI compute until the site's post-bankruptcy status is confirmed and its current use is independently verified.
